cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Let the Callback Claim Credit
cards.instruction: Get recognition by returning to an early overlooked contribution when its importance becomes undeniable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That cross of tape I copied from yours is still on the curtain. You called it untidy.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine marked where a chair goes on the floor. Yours is stuck across a torn seam.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, marking the weak point. Leave it until the finale's over.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The seam's split farther. Your tape is the only thing holding the two halves together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then thank the person who left the untidy cross there. Say that before you ask me to peel it off.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copied tape cross was dismissed; B2 exposes floor-mark versus curtain seam; A3 pretends weak-point marking and A5 claims credit once B4 makes its structural value undeniable.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 torn seam gives A3 reason to leave tape; B4 further split proves the accidental contribution, prompting A5 named thanks.

relationship.evidence: B4 notices an actual worsening tear and identifies what still holds it.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 demonstrated benefit to demand recognition before the earlier cosmetic objection returns.

specificity.evidence: A1 curtain tape and B2 seam/floor contrast make the misuse legible; B4 limited seam support is more plausible than tape holding an entire curtain aloft.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 peel-it-off callback is directed to the original critic rather than an abstract claim of ingenuity.
